items.prompt: Where does Aziz live?
items.passage:
My name is Aziz and I live in Samarkand with my family. There are five people in my family: my mother Dilnoza, my father Rustam, my sister Malika, my little brother Jasur and me. We are very busy during the week, but the weekend is special for us.

On Saturday morning we get up at eight o'clock. My father makes breakfast. He makes eggs and bread for everyone. After breakfast, my mother and Malika go to the market. They buy fruit, rice and meat. My brother and I clean our room and help my father in the garden. We have many apple trees and some flowers. The flowers are red and yellow.

In the afternoon we visit my grandmother. She lives near the park, only ten minutes from our house. She cooks plov for us, and it is very good. We eat together and talk about school and work. Then Jasur plays football with our cousins in the park.

On Sunday we stay at home. We do not go to school or to work. My mother reads a book, and my father watches a film. Malika and I play cards. In the evening we all walk by the river. It is a quiet and beautiful place. We come home at seven o'clock and have tea.

I love our weekends. We are together and we are happy. I think family time is the best time of the week.

items.prompt: Where does the grandmother live?
items.passage:
My grandmother lives in a small village near Fergana. Her name is Zulfiya, and she is seventy years old. I visit her every summer. I love her house very much.

The house is old, but it is clean and warm. There are four rooms: a kitchen, a living room and two bedrooms. In the living room there is a big carpet on the floor. The carpet is red and blue. There is also a small table and a TV, but my grandmother does not watch it often. She likes the radio more.

Behind the house there is a garden. There are two cherry trees, a vine and many vegetables. My grandmother grows tomatoes, onions and carrots. In the morning we get vegetables from the garden and make a salad. There are also six chickens in the yard. I give them water and bread every day. My favourite chicken is white and its name is Oq.

In the evening we sit outside on a wooden bed called a sufa. My grandmother makes green tea and puts sweets on a plate. She tells me stories about her childhood. Sometimes she sings an old song. I do not know all the words, but I love the music.

There is no shop in the village, so my grandmother makes bread in a tandoor. The bread is hot and soft. It smells wonderful. I eat three pieces and she laughs. This house is my second home.

items.prompt: Where does Gulnora work?
items.passage:
Gulnora is a nurse in a big hospital in Tashkent. She is thirty-two years old and she has two children. Her job is hard, but she loves it. She helps sick people every day.

Gulnora gets up at five o'clock in the morning. She makes tea and wakes her children at six. Her husband takes them to school. Gulnora goes to work by bus. The bus ride takes forty minutes. She starts work at seven o'clock.

First, she checks the patients. She takes their temperature and asks, "How are you today?" Some patients are old, and some are very young. There is a little boy named Bobur in room twelve. He has a bad leg. Gulnora always brings him a book, and he smiles. She gives medicine to the patients at nine o'clock and again at two o'clock.

At twelve o'clock she has lunch with two other nurses. They eat in a small room. Gulnora usually has soup and bread. She cannot sit for a long time because the phone rings often. There are many new patients on Mondays.

She finishes work at four o'clock. At home she cooks dinner, helps her children with homework and tells them a story. She goes to bed at ten. Gulnora says, "I am tired in the evening, but I am happy. I help people, and that is important."

items.prompt: Where did Sardor's family move?
items.passage:
Last month my family moved to a new flat in Namangan. My name is Sardor and I am twelve years old. Our old flat was very small, and there was only one bedroom. Now we have three bedrooms, and I have my own room. I am very happy.

The new flat is on the fourth floor. There is a lift in the building, but it is often broken. So we usually use the stairs. In the flat there is a big kitchen with a window. In the kitchen there is a table for six people. My mother loves this room. She says, "At last I can cook for all the family."

Moving day was very busy. My uncle Anvar came with his small truck. We put the beds, the sofa and many boxes in it. My sister Zarina was careful with the plates. I carried my books. There were twenty boxes of books, and my father laughed at me. The work took six hours. In the evening we were very hungry, so we ate pizza on the floor.

There are good things near the new flat. There is a school across the road, and there is a small park behind the building. I can walk to school in five minutes. I can also play football in the park with my new friends.

The flat is not perfect because the neighbours upstairs are noisy. But we love our new home.

items.prompt: Where does Kamola live?
items.passage:
Dear Emma,

Thank you for your letter. It was a great surprise! I am happy to be your pen friend. Let me tell you about myself and my family.

My name is Kamola, and I am eleven years old. I live in Bukhara, a very old city in Uzbekistan. There are six people in my house: my parents, my grandfather, my brother and my sister. My grandfather is eighty years old. He is funny and kind. He has a long white beard, and he wears a small hat every day.

My father is a driver. He works in the city centre and comes home late. My mother is a teacher. She teaches English at a small school. That is why I can write to you in English! My brother Otabek is fifteen, and he plays the guitar very well. My sister Madina is only four. She likes drawing and she draws cats everywhere.

I go to school from Monday to Saturday. My favourite subjects are English and art. After school I do my homework and help my mother in the kitchen. On Fridays I go to a swimming pool with my friend Sevara.

Please write to me about your family and your town. Do you have a pet? I have a white cat. Her name is Luna.

With love,
Kamola

My mother is the busiest person I know. Her name is Barno, and she has three jobs: she is a mother, a shop assistant and a student. I am very proud of her.

My mother gets up at half past five. First she makes breakfast for my father, my sister and me. Then she packs my lunch. She always puts an apple and a sandwich in my bag. At seven o'clock she takes my sister Dilya to kindergarten. After that she walks to her shop. It is a clothes shop in the centre of town.

She works there from eight o'clock to three o'clock. She is polite and she smiles at everybody. Many customers know her name. They say, "Barno is the best!" On her lunch break she does not rest. She calls my grandmother and asks, "Are you well? Do you need anything?"

At half past three she picks up Dilya. Then she goes home and cooks dinner. We eat at six o'clock. After dinner she washes the dishes, and I dry them. At eight o'clock she opens her books. She studies business at a small college. She has classes only on Tuesday and Thursday evenings, so on other days she studies at home.

She goes to bed very late, at eleven o'clock. I say to her, "Mum, you are amazing!" She laughs and says, "Thank you, my dear."

items.prompt: When does the family have dinner at the grandparents' house?
items.passage:
Every Friday evening our whole family has dinner at my grandparents' house. My name is Lola. I am nine years old and I love Friday dinners.

We arrive at six o'clock. My uncle Farhod and his wife Shahlo are already there with their baby son. The baby is called Timur, and he is only eight months old. He has big brown eyes and two small teeth. Everybody wants to hold him.

My grandmother cooks all day. On the table there is a big plate of plov, a green salad, fresh bread and a bowl of yoghurt. For dessert there is a sweet melon. My grandmother says, "Eat, eat! There is plenty of food!" I always eat too much.

My grandfather sits at the head of the table. He is a quiet man, but he likes to ask questions. He asks me, "What do you learn at school, Lola?" Then he listens carefully. My father tells funny stories about his work. My mother and my aunt talk about clothes and shops. My cousins and I laugh a lot.

After dinner the men drink tea and the women wash the dishes. The children play a game in the garden. We go home at nine o'clock. In the car I am sleepy, and I fall asleep before we arrive. Friday dinner is the best part of my week.

items.prompt: Behruz is ___ years old.
items.passage:
I have a little brother. His name is Behruz and he is five years old. He is small, but he has a very big voice! I am his big sister, and my name is Sabina. I am thirteen.

Behruz has short black hair and a round face. He is always happy, and he talks all day. In the morning he wakes me up at six o'clock and says, "Sabina, I am hungry!" I make him milk and toast with honey. He eats very slowly because he plays with his food.

He loves cars. In his room there are fifty small cars. They are red, blue, yellow and green. He puts them in a long line on the floor and says their names. His favourite car is a small red fire truck. He takes it everywhere, even to the bathroom. At night he sleeps with it under his pillow.

He also loves animals. He wants a dog, but my mother says no. She says, "We live in a flat, and a dog needs a garden." So Behruz has two fish. Their names are Bubble and Splash. He feeds them every morning and talks to them.

Sometimes Behruz is naughty. Last week he drew a picture on the wall with my pen. My mother was not happy. But then he said, "I am sorry, I love you," and she smiled. I think my little brother is a small hero.

items.prompt: Every ___ is cleaning day.
items.passage:
Every Saturday is cleaning day in our house. My name is Jahongir and I live with my parents and my two sisters. Our flat is not big, but it gets dirty very fast, so we all help.

We start at nine o'clock. My mother gives everybody a job. She is like a small boss! My father cleans the windows and the balcony. My older sister, Nodira, washes the kitchen floor. My younger sister, Kamila, is only seven, so she waters the flowers and puts her toys in a box. My job is the living room. I put the books on the shelf, I take the dust from the table and I clean the carpet with a machine.

My mother does the hardest work. She washes the clothes and the curtains. There is a big washing machine in the bathroom, but it is very old and very loud. When it works, we cannot hear the radio. Then she hangs the clothes on the balcony. In summer they are dry in two hours.

At twelve o'clock the flat is clean and shiny. We are tired and hungry. Dad makes a big pot of soup, and we eat it with fresh bread. After lunch we rest.

I do not like cleaning, but I like the result. A clean room feels good. In the evening I sit on the sofa and read my book. It is very quiet and fresh.

items.prompt: Where did Ulugbek's family go on holiday?
items.answer: To a lake in the mountains
items.passage:
Last summer my family went on holiday to a lake in the mountains. My name is Ulugbek and I am ten years old. We went for one week, and it was the best week of the year.

We left home at five o'clock in the morning. My father drove, and my mother sat next to him with the map. My grandmother came with us too, and she brought a big bag of food. There were cakes, apples, cheese and a bottle of cold tea. My sister and I slept in the back of the car for two hours.

The lake was very beautiful. The water was clear and blue, and there were high green mountains around it. We stayed in a small wooden house near the water. There was no TV and no internet. At first I was not happy, but then I loved it.

Every day we did something fun. On Monday we swam in the lake. The water was cold! On Tuesday my father and I caught three fish, and my grandmother cooked them for dinner. On Wednesday we walked up a small mountain. From the top we saw sheep and horses. My sister took a lot of photos.

In the evenings we made a fire and sang songs. There were thousands of stars in the sky. I never see so many stars at home. On the last day I was sad. I said, "Can we come back next year?" My father said, "Of course!"

We left home at five o'clock in the morning. My father drove, and my mother sat next to him with the map. My grandmother came with us too, and she brought a big bag of food. There were cakes, apples, cheese and a bottle of cold tea. My sister and I slept in the back of the car for two hours.

The lake was very beautiful. The water was clear and blue, and there were high green mountains around it. We stayed in a small wooden house near the water. There was no TV and no internet. At first I was not happy, but then I loved it.

Every day we did something fun. On Monday we swam in the lake. The water was cold! On Tuesday my father and I caught three fish, and my grandmother cooked them for dinner. On Wednesday we walked up a small mountain. From the top we saw sheep and horses. My sister took a lot of photos.

In the evenings we made a fire and sang songs. There were thousands of stars in the sky. I never see so many stars at home. On the last day I was sad. I said, "Can we come back next year?" My father said, "Of course!"

items.prompt: What is Hamid's job?
items.passage:
My father is a builder. His name is Hamid, and he builds houses and small shops. I am Nargiza, and I am eleven. I think my father has an interesting job.

He gets up very early, at half past four, because the work starts at six o'clock. He drinks a cup of black tea and eats a piece of bread. Then he takes his yellow hat and his boots and goes out. He travels to work by an old white bus. Today he is building a new house on the edge of our town.

My father works with five other men. Their boss is Mr Karimov. Every day they carry bricks, mix cement and put up walls. It is hot in summer and cold in winter. My father says, "It is hard work, but I like to see a house grow." When a house is ready, he takes me to see it. I am always amazed.

At noon the men stop for lunch. They sit under a tree and eat bread, boiled eggs and tomatoes. My mother puts the lunch in a blue box for my father. Sometimes she adds a small sweet for him.

He comes home at five o'clock and he is very dirty. First he takes a shower, then he plays with my little brother. On Sundays he does not work. He rests and sometimes he fixes our chairs and doors. He can fix everything!

items.prompt: The building has ___ flats.
items.passage:
We live in a big building with twenty flats. I like our neighbours very much. My name is Dilshod, and I want to tell you about them.

On the first floor there lives an old man called Mr Ergash. He is seventy-five and he lives alone. He has a green parrot named Chiroq. The parrot can say "Hello" and "Good morning". Every day I stop at his door and talk to Chiroq. Mr Ergash always gives me a sweet.

On the second floor there is a family with four children. The mother is called Aziza, and she is a hairdresser. The children are noisy, but they are very friendly. Sometimes we play football together in the yard. The youngest girl is called Aysha and she is only three. She cannot run fast, but she tries.

Our flat is on the third floor, and next door there lives a young doctor, Doctor Sherzod. He is single and very busy. He works at night, so in the day he sleeps. We are quiet in the afternoon because of him. When my mother is ill, he comes and helps for free. We are lucky to have him.

On the top floor there is a nice lady called Mrs Hilola. She bakes cakes every Sunday and gives a piece to everybody in the building. Her apple cake is the best in town.

Good neighbours are like a second family.

items.prompt: Whose birthday was it?
items.passage:
Last Saturday was my mother's birthday. She is forty years old now. My name is Rayhon, and my brother Doniyor and I wanted to give her a big surprise.

We planned everything with our father one week before. He said, "Your mother thinks we forget her birthday. Let's make a party!" So we called her sister, Aunt Mavluda, and my grandmother. They agreed to come at four o'clock. My mother was at work until three, so we had enough time.

On Saturday morning my father took my mother to the market. She did not know the reason. Meanwhile Doniyor and I made decorations. We cut paper hearts and stars and put them on the walls. We also blew up twenty balloons. They were pink, white and blue. Aunt Mavluda came early and brought a huge chocolate cake with forty small candles.

At half past four my mother came home. All the lights were off. She opened the door and we all shouted, "Happy birthday!" She was so surprised that she dropped her bag. Then she began to cry and laugh at the same time. "I cannot believe it," she said.

We sang a song and she blew out the candles. My present was a small blue scarf, and she put it on at once. We ate cake, drank tea and danced. It was the happiest day of the year for our family.

Last Saturday was my mother's birthday. She is forty years old now. My name is Rayhon, and my brother Doniyor and I wanted to give her a big surprise.

We planned everything with our father one week before. He said, "Your mother thinks we forget her birthday. Let's make a party!" So we called her sister, Aunt Mavluda, and my grandmother. They agreed to come at four o'clock. My mother was at work until three, so we had enough time.

On Saturday morning my father took my mother to the market. She did not know the reason. Meanwhile Doniyor and I made decorations. We cut paper hearts and stars and put them on the walls. We also blew up twenty balloons. They were pink, white and blue. Aunt Mavluda came early and brought a huge chocolate cake with forty small candles.

At half past four my mother came home. All the lights were off. She opened the door and we all shouted, "Happy birthday!" She was so surprised that she dropped her bag. Then she began to cry and laugh at the same time. "I cannot believe it," she said.

We sang a song and she blew out the candles. My present was a small blue scarf, and she put it on at once. We ate cake, drank tea and danced. It was the happiest day of the year for our family.

items.prompt: Where is the family album?
items.answer: On the top shelf of a cupboard
items.passage:
In our living room there is an old brown cupboard. On the top shelf there is a big family album. My name is Shahzod. On rainy days I take the album and look at the photos with my grandmother.

The first photo is black and white. It shows my grandparents on their wedding day. My grandmother is young and beautiful. She wears a long white dress and holds red flowers. My grandfather is thin and tall, and he has a big smile. They were only twenty years old.

The next page has photos of my father as a child. He is four years old and sits on a small horse. He looks afraid, and my grandmother always laughs when she sees this photo. There is also a photo of my father at school. He wears a white shirt and a blue tie.

My favourite photo is of my parents on a boat. It was their honeymoon in Turkey. They are young and happy, and the sea is bright blue behind them. My mother has long hair in this photo. Now it is short.

The last pages are for me and my sister. There is a photo of me on my first birthday with cake all over my face. My sister Zebo says, "Please do not show this photo to my friends!"

I love our album. It tells the story of our family, and I want to add many new photos to it.
options: On the top shelf of a cupboard

items.prompt: How old is Muhammad's grandfather?
items.passage:
My grandfather knows a thousand stories. His name is Tohir, and he is eighty-two years old. I am Muhammad, and I am eight. Every evening after dinner I sit next to him and ask, "Grandpa, tell me a story!"

He sits in his big green chair and puts on his glasses. First he drinks a little tea. Then he starts: "A long time ago, when I was a boy..." I love these words. They mean a new adventure begins.

My favourite story is about his first job. When he was fourteen, he worked on a farm near a river. He got up at four o'clock every morning and gave food to the cows. His boss was an old woman, and she had a very loud voice. One day a small cow ran away. My grandfather ran after it for three hours. At last he found it in a garden. The old woman gave him a big watermelon as a prize.

Another story is about his bicycle. It was his first bicycle and it was red. He paid for it with his own money. He rode it to school every day. One winter day he fell into the snow, and everyone laughed.

Sometimes his stories are sad, but most of them are funny. When I ask if they are true, he smiles and says, "A good story is always a little bit true."

I want to remember them all. Tomorrow I will bring my notebook and write them down.

My grandfather knows a thousand stories. His name is Tohir, and he is eighty-two years old. I am Muhammad, and I am eight. Every evening after dinner I sit next to him and ask, "Grandpa, tell me a story!"

He sits in his big green chair and puts on his glasses. First he drinks a little tea. Then he starts: "A long time ago, when I was a boy..." I love these words. They mean a new adventure begins.

My favourite story is about his first job. When he was fourteen, he worked on a farm near a river. He got up at four o'clock every morning and gave food to the cows. His boss was an old woman, and she had a very loud voice. One day a small cow ran away. My grandfather ran after it for three hours. At last he found it in a garden. The old woman gave him a big watermelon as a prize.

Another story is about his bicycle. It was his first bicycle and it was red. He paid for it with his own money. He rode it to school every day. One winter day he fell into the snow, and everyone laughed.

Sometimes his stories are sad, but most of them are funny. When I ask if they are true, he smiles and says, "A good story is always a little bit true."

I want to remember them all. Tomorrow I will bring my notebook and write them down.

items.prompt: How old is Aziz?
items.passage:
My name is Aziz. I am seven years old, and today is my first day at school. I wake up at six o'clock. My mother makes eggs and bread for breakfast, but I do not eat much. I am a little afraid.

My school is in Samarkand. It is not far from my house. My father walks with me, and we carry my new blue bag. In the bag there are two books, three pens and a small lunch box. My grandmother puts an apple in it.

There are many children in the yard. Some of them are crying, and some are laughing. A tall woman says hello to us. She is my teacher, and her name is Mrs Karimova. She has a kind smile. I feel better.

Our classroom is on the second floor. There are twenty desks and a big green board. I sit next to a boy called Bobur. He has a red pencil case. He says, "Do you like football?" I say, "Yes, I do." Now we are friends.

In the first lesson, we learn the names of everyone in the class. Then we draw a picture of our family. I draw my mother, my father and my little sister Madina. At twelve o'clock, we go home. My mother asks, "Do you like school?" I say, "Yes! I want to go again tomorrow."

items.prompt: What time do the girls meet?
items.passage:
My best friend is Malika. We are both ten years old, and we are in the same class. We meet every morning at the school gate at eight o'clock. She lives near my house, so we walk together.

Malika has long black hair and big brown eyes. She is very funny. She can make jokes in every lesson, but the teacher is not angry because the jokes are good. She is also kind. When I am sad, she gives me a sweet and says, "Don't worry."

We like the same things. We both love drawing and cats. Malika has two cats, Mimi and Tom. I have one fish. On Saturdays I go to her house. Her mother cooks plov, and we eat it in the garden. After lunch we play cards or draw pictures of the cats.

But we are also different. Malika is very good at maths, and I am not. I am good at English, and she is not. So she helps me with numbers, and I help her with words. This is a good way to learn.

Last year, Malika moved to a bigger house, but the new house is only five minutes from mine. I was happy. A best friend is a person who listens to you, laughs with you and never forgets your birthday. Malika is all of these things.

items.prompt: How many times a week do they have English?
items.passage:
We have English class three times a week: on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. Our teacher is Mr Brown. He is from London, and he is thirty-five years old. He is tall and he wears glasses. He speaks slowly, so we understand him.

There are fifteen students in our class. Our classroom is small, but it is bright. There are pictures of animals on the walls and a big map of the world. On the teacher's desk there is a small radio. We listen to songs and short stories on it.

Every lesson starts in the same way. Mr Brown says, "Good morning, everyone! How are you today?" We answer, "We are fine, thank you." Then we do a short game. Yesterday, we played a game with colours. I said, "The sky is blue and the grass is green." Everyone clapped.

After the game, we open our books. We read a text and answer questions. Sometimes we work in pairs. I sit with Nigora. She is quiet, but she knows many words. We write new words in our notebooks and learn them at home.

On Fridays, we have a spelling test. There are ten words. Last Friday I got nine right. Mr Brown said, "Well done, Sardor!" I was very happy. I love English because it is fun, and I want to visit London one day.

There are fifteen students in our class. Our classroom is small, but it is bright. There are pictures of animals on the walls and a big map of the world. On the teacher's desk there is a small radio. We listen to songs and short stories on it.

Every lesson starts in the same way. Mr Brown says, "Good morning, everyone! How are you today?" We answer, "We are fine, thank you." Then we do a short game. Yesterday, we played a game with colours. I said, "The sky is blue and the grass is green." Everyone clapped.

After the game, we open our books. We read a text and answer questions. Sometimes we work in pairs. I sit with Nigora. She is quiet, but she knows many words. We write new words in our notebooks and learn them at home.

On Fridays, we have a spelling test. There are ten words. Last Friday I got nine right. Mr Brown said, "Well done, Sardor!" I was very happy. I love English because it is fun, and I want to visit London one day.

items.prompt: Where did the class go?
items.passage:
Last Thursday, our class went on a school trip to the zoo in Tashkent. We were very excited. We met at the school at seven thirty in the morning. There were twenty-four children and three teachers. Our bus was big and yellow.

The trip took one hour. On the bus, we sang songs, and my friend Jasur told funny stories. Our teacher, Ms Umarova, counted the children two times. She said, "Please stay with your group and do not run."

At the zoo, we saw many animals. First we visited the monkeys. They were very noisy, and one monkey took a banana from a boy's hand. We all laughed. Then we saw the lions. They were sleeping under a tree, so we were quiet. My favourite animal was the elephant. It was big and grey, and it was drinking water with its nose.

At twelve o'clock, we had lunch on the grass. I had bread, cheese and a bottle of juice. Jasur forgot his lunch, so I gave him half of my cheese. He said, "Thank you, you are a good friend."

After lunch, we went to the small shop. I bought a postcard with a picture of a tiger for my grandfather. We left the zoo at three o'clock. On the way home, many children were tired and slept on the bus. It was a great day, and I want to go again.

items.prompt: What is the first exam?
items.passage:
Today is exam day. I am Gulnora, and I am fourteen. My first exam is maths, and it starts at nine o'clock. I did not sleep well last night because I was very nervous. I woke up at six, and I had tea and a slice of bread.

My brother Timur says, "Don't worry. You studied a lot." He is right. For two weeks, I studied every evening for two hours. My friend Zarina came to my house on Sunday, and we practised together. She is clever, and she explained the hard questions to me.

At school, there are many students in the corridor. Some of them are reading their notes. Some are talking quietly. I am holding two pens, a ruler and a small bottle of water. The rules are simple. We cannot use phones, and we cannot talk during the exam.

At nine o'clock, the teacher opens the door. We go in and sit at separate desks. There are twenty questions on the paper, and we have one hour and thirty minutes. I read the paper slowly. The first questions are easy. I smile. Question fifteen is difficult, so I leave it and go on.

At ten thirty, the teacher says, "Stop writing, please." I put my pen down. I think I did well. After the exam, Zarina and I buy ice cream. Tomorrow we have English, but today we are free and happy.

items.prompt: What does Mrs Olga teach?
items.passage:
My favourite teacher is Mrs Olga. She teaches science, and she is forty-five years old. She has short grey hair and a warm voice. She wears a green coat in winter, and everyone knows her by it.

Mrs Olga is not like other teachers. She does not only read from the book. She brings things to class. Last week, she brought a small plant, a magnifying glass and a bowl of water. We looked at the leaves and learned how plants drink. It was very interesting.

She is also very patient. When we do not understand, she explains again and again. She never shouts. She says, "A mistake is a good friend, because we learn from it." I like this sentence a lot, and I wrote it on the first page of my notebook.

After lessons, Mrs Olga has a science club. It is on Tuesdays at three o'clock. There are twelve children in the club. We make small experiments, for example a volcano from soda and vinegar. Last month, our volcano was so big that the floor became wet, and we all laughed.

Mrs Olga lives near the school, and she has a dog called Max. Sometimes Max comes to the school yard, and the children are very happy. I want to be a teacher like her one day.

items.prompt: What time does the canteen open?
items.passage:
Our school canteen is big and clean. It opens at ten o'clock, and we have our break at ten thirty. There are fifteen tables, and each table has six chairs. On the wall there is a menu with the food of the week.

The canteen has two cooks. Their names are Aunt Zulfiya and Mr Hasan. Aunt Zulfiya is round and smiling, and she always says, "Eat well, children!" Mr Hasan makes the best soup in the city, in my opinion.

Every day the food is different. On Monday, we have rice with chicken. On Tuesday, there is pasta with meat. On Wednesday, we eat fish and potatoes. My favourite day is Thursday, because there are samsas. They are hot and cost two thousand som each. A glass of tea costs five hundred som.

I usually sit with my friends Kamila and Otabek. Kamila does not eat meat, so she takes vegetables and bread. Otabek eats a lot. He can eat three samsas in five minutes. We talk, laugh and share our news.

There are some rules in the canteen. We must wash our hands first. We must stand in a line, and we must not push. After lunch, we put our plates on a big table near the door. The canteen is not a fancy place, but it is warm and the food is good. I like it.

items.prompt: Where is Daniel from?
items.passage:
Last Monday, a new student came to our class. His name is Daniel, and he is from Canada. He is eleven years old. He has fair hair and blue eyes, and he is quite tall. Our teacher, Mr Aliyev, said, "Please be kind to Daniel. He cannot speak much Uzbek yet."

Daniel looked shy. He sat at the back of the class and did not say a word. At break, he stood alone near the window. I felt sorry for him. I went to him and said, "Hello! My name is Sherzod. Do you want to play football?" He smiled and said, "Yes, please."

Daniel is very good at football. He can run fast and he scored two goals that day. After the game, all the boys wanted to be his friends. We showed him the school. We took him to the library, the canteen and the gym. He liked the gym best.

Now Daniel is learning Uzbek. He knows ten words already, for example salom, rahmat and non. In return, we help him with the lessons, and he teaches us some English words. He lives with his parents in a flat near the park, and his father works at a bank.

This Saturday, Daniel is coming to my house for lunch. My mother is going to cook manti. I think he will love it. I am happy that we have a new friend.

items.passage:
I have a problem. I have too much homework! Today is Tuesday, and I have homework in four subjects. There are ten maths exercises, a page of English words, a short story to read and a drawing for art class. I get home at four o'clock, and I am very tired.

First, I have a snack and a glass of milk. Then I sit at my desk. My room is quiet, but my little brother Ali is very noisy. He plays with his toy car and makes loud sounds. I say, "Ali, please be quiet!" He does not listen.

My maths homework is the hardest. I do the first five exercises, but the sixth is too difficult. I try three times, and the answer is wrong every time. I phone my friend Feruza. She says, "I can help you. Come to my house." Her house is only two streets away, so I go there.

Feruza explains the exercise in a simple way. Now I understand! We finish the maths in twenty minutes. Then we do the English words together. Her mother brings us tea and biscuits.

I come back home at seven o'clock and finish the drawing. I draw a blue bird on a tree. My father says, "It is beautiful." I go to bed at nine. My plan for next time is simple. I must start earlier, and I must not wait until the end.

items.prompt: When was sports day?
items.passage:
Sports day is the best day of the school year. This year, it was on Friday, the fifth of May. The weather was sunny and warm. We all wore white T-shirts, and each team had a different colour on its hat. My team was the red team.

There were many games. First, there was a running race for the small children. A little boy fell down, but he stood up and finished the race. Everyone clapped and shouted. Then the older children played football and volleyball. Our red team won the volleyball game by two points.

I took part in the long jump. My friend Nilufar jumped three metres, and I jumped two metres and eighty centimetres. She won, and I was second. I was a bit sad, but I was also proud of her. Nilufar is the best athlete in our school.

At twelve o'clock, we had a break. Parents brought cold water, apples and sandwiches. My father came with my grandfather, and they sat under a big tree. They took many photos of me.

The last game was tug of war. Our team pulled very hard, but the blue team won. We were tired, wet and happy. At the end, the headmaster gave a cup to the blue team and a small medal to every child. I put my medal on the wall in my room.

items.prompt: Where is the library?
items.passage:
Our school library is my favourite place. It is on the first floor, next to the music room. It is open from eight in the morning to four in the afternoon, from Monday to Saturday. The librarian is Mrs Saida. She is old, but she is very nice.

There are about five thousand books in the library. There are storybooks, science books, dictionaries and also some old newspapers. In the corner there is a soft red sofa, and I like to sit there. There are also six computers, but we can use them only for one hour.

Every student can take two books home. We keep them for two weeks. If we need more time, we can ask Mrs Saida, and she says yes. But if we lose a book, we must buy a new one. Last year, a boy lost a book about dinosaurs, and he was very sorry.

Last week, I read a book about space. In the book, there are many pictures of planets. I learned that Jupiter is the biggest planet. Now I want to be an astronaut. I told my friend Rustam, and he laughed. Then he borrowed the book too.

The library is very quiet. We must not eat or shout there. We can only whisper. For me, this is the best part. I can think, read and feel calm. I go there every day after lunch.

items.prompt: On which days does the writer go to school?
items.passage:
This is my timetable. I go to school from Monday to Saturday, and each day we have five or six lessons. The first lesson starts at eight thirty, and every lesson is forty-five minutes long. We have a break of ten minutes after each lesson and a long break at eleven thirty.

Monday is a busy day. We have maths, Uzbek, English, history and PE. I like PE, but I do not like history, because there are many dates to learn. On Tuesday, we have science, art and music. I love art. Our teacher says my pictures are colourful.

Wednesday is my favourite day, because we have two English lessons and a computer lesson. On Thursday, we have maths again, and then geography. On Friday, there is a short day. We have only four lessons, and we finish at twelve fifteen. I go home and play with my cousin Anvar.

Saturday is special. We do not have difficult subjects. We have a class hour, a reading lesson and clubs. I go to the chess club, and my sister goes to the dance club.

I keep my timetable on the wall above my desk. Every evening, I look at it and put the books for the next day into my bag. My mother says it is a good habit. I think she is right, because now I never forget my books.

items.prompt: What was the concert for?
items.passage:
Last Friday, our school had a concert for Teachers' Day. It was at five o'clock in the big hall. There were about two hundred people: students, parents and teachers. The hall was full of flowers and balloons.

I was in the school choir. We are twenty children, and we practised for a month, three times a week. Our music teacher, Mr Farhod, played the piano. He is very strict, but he is also funny. Before the concert, he said, "Smile and sing loudly. You can do it!"

I was very nervous. My hands were cold, and my heart was fast. My friend Laylo was next to me. She whispered, "Look at the back wall, not at the people." I did that, and it helped.

We sang three songs. The first one was in Uzbek, the second was in English and the last was a funny song about a cat. After the last song, everyone clapped for a long time. I saw my mother in the second row. She was smiling and she had tears in her eyes.

After our choir, a boy played the guitar, and two girls danced. A small girl read a poem. At the end, the headmaster thanked all the teachers and gave them flowers.

It was a lovely evening. At home, my father said, "You sang very well." I want to sing in the next concert too.

items.prompt: How old is the grandmother?
items.passage:
My grandmother Halima is seventy years old, and she is learning to read. She did not go to school when she was a girl. Her family was poor, and she had to work in the fields. Now she has time, and she wants to learn.

Every afternoon, she comes to my room at four o'clock. I am her teacher! I am ten years old, but I know the letters well. We sit at the table, and I put a small book in front of her. It is a book with big letters and many pictures.

At first, it was difficult. She could not read the letters at all. Now she can read short words like cat, sun and home. Last week, she read a whole sentence: "The sun is hot." She was so happy that she cried. I hugged her and said, "Well done, Grandma!"

She is not fast, but she never stops. She has a notebook, and she writes ten new words in it every day. Her writing is big and not very straight, but I can read it. She says, "My eyes are old, but my head is young."

My grandmother has a dream. She wants to read the letters from my uncle, who lives in Russia. She also wants to read old poems. I think she can do it. I help her every day, and I am proud of her.

items.prompt: What is the room number?
items.passage:
On Wednesdays, we have a computer lesson in room number twelve. There are fifteen computers in the room, and two students share each computer. I sit with my friend Madina. Our teacher is Mr Anvar. He is young, and he always wears a black shirt.

Today's lesson was about typing. Mr Anvar said, "Typing fast is a very useful skill. Please put your fingers on the keyboard like this." He showed us a picture on the screen. Then we opened a program and typed a short text about our families.

It was not easy. I made many mistakes, and I typed very slowly. Madina is much faster than me. She can type thirty words in one minute. I can type only ten. But Mr Anvar told me, "Don't worry, Karim. Practise a little every day, and you will get better."

After typing, we learned about safety on the internet. Mr Anvar gave us three rules. First, never tell strangers your name or address. Second, never give anyone your password. Third, ask an adult if you see something strange. We wrote these rules in our notebooks.

At the end of the lesson, we played a game on the computer. We had to find animals on a map. My team found twelve animals, and we won. I love computer lessons because they are fun. At home, I do not have a computer, so this lesson is very special for me.

items.prompt: Where does Dilnoza go every Sunday?
items.passage:
Every Sunday, my mother and I go to the big market in Samarkand. We leave home at seven o'clock in the morning because the market is very busy later. My name is Dilnoza and I am nine years old. I like the market because it is full of colours and smells.

First we go to the bread seller. He has a big round oven, and his bread is always hot. My mother buys two loaves from him. Then we walk to the fruit tables. There are red apples, yellow melons and green grapes. My mother likes grapes, but I like melons. The fruit seller is a kind old woman. She always gives me a small piece of melon to taste. It is very sweet.

After the fruit, we buy vegetables. We need onions, carrots and potatoes for dinner. My mother asks the price and the man says, "Carrots are three thousand sums for one kilo." She buys two kilos. The market is noisy, and people shout, laugh and talk. A little boy sells flowers near the gate. Today my mother buys a small bunch of white flowers for our table.

We go home at ten o'clock. My bag is heavy, but I am happy. At home, my grandmother helps us wash the vegetables. In the evening, we cook a big dinner and the whole family eats together. I think the Sunday market is the best part of my week.

items.prompt: What is the name of the restaurant?
items.passage:
My favourite restaurant is called Silk Road. It is near my school in Tashkent. We go there on my father's birthday and on other special days. The restaurant is not big, but it is very clean and warm. There are ten tables, and each table has a small lamp and a green cloth.

The waiter is a friendly man. His name is Aziz. He wears a white shirt and a black hat. He always says, "Welcome, my friends!" Then he gives us the menu. My father orders lagman, which is a soup with long noodles, meat and vegetables. My mother likes fish and rice. My little sister Madina eats only chips and chicken. I always choose samsa because it is hot and has tasty meat inside.

The food comes after fifteen minutes. We drink green tea with our dinner, and Madina has orange juice. The music is soft, and people talk quietly. On the wall there are pictures of old cities like Bukhara and Khiva. I like to look at them while we eat.

The prices are not high. A big dinner for four people costs about two hundred thousand sums. After dinner, Aziz brings a small cake for my father, and we sing a song. Then we say thank you and go home. I hope we can come back soon.

items.prompt: How old is Grandma Halima?
items.passage:
On Friday I go to my grandmother's house. Her name is Halima and she is sixty-five years old. She lives in a small house with a big garden in Fergana. On Fridays we cook plov together. Plov is a famous dish in Uzbekistan. It has rice, meat, carrots and onions.

First, Grandma puts a big black pot on the fire. She puts oil in the pot. When the oil is hot, she adds the onions. I cut the carrots into long thin pieces. I must be careful with the knife! Grandma says, "Slowly, Gulnora, slowly." Then she puts the meat in the pot. After ten minutes, she adds the carrots and some salt.

Next, we wash the rice three times. Grandma adds the rice and some warm water. She puts one whole garlic in the middle of the pot. Then we close the pot and wait for forty minutes. The kitchen smells wonderful. My grandfather comes in and says, "I am very hungry!"

At one o'clock, the plov is ready. We put it on a large plate and take it to the table in the garden. We also have a salad of tomatoes and onions. All my cousins come, and there are eight people at the table. Everyone says the plov is delicious. I am proud because I helped. Grandma smiles and says I am a good cook.

First, Grandma puts a big black pot on the fire. She puts oil in the pot. When the oil is hot, she adds the onions. I cut the carrots into long thin pieces. I must be careful with the knife! Grandma says, "Slowly, Gulnora, slowly." Then she puts the meat in the pot. After ten minutes, she adds the carrots and some salt.

Next, we wash the rice three times. Grandma adds the rice and some warm water. She puts one whole garlic in the middle of the pot. Then we close the pot and wait for forty minutes. The kitchen smells wonderful. My grandfather comes in and says, "I am very hungry!"

At one o'clock, the plov is ready. We put it on a large plate and take it to the table in the garden. We also have a salad of tomatoes and onions. All my cousins come, and there are eight people at the table. Everyone says the plov is delicious. I am proud because I helped. Grandma smiles and says I am a good cook.

items.prompt: How old is Rustam?
items.passage:
My name is Rustam and I am twelve years old. My mother is very busy on Saturday, so she writes a shopping list for me. I can go to the shop alone. The shop is only five minutes from our flat. My mother gives me twenty thousand sums and the list.

The list says: one bottle of milk, six eggs, a kilo of rice, two tomatoes and a small bag of sugar. At the end of the list, my mother writes, "Buy one sweet for yourself." I smile. I put the money in my pocket and I go.

In the shop, there are many people. First, I find the milk. It is in the cold place at the back. Then I look for eggs. The eggs are on a shelf near the door. I take a box of six. The rice and sugar are on the next shelf. But I cannot find the tomatoes. I ask a woman who works in the shop. She says, "Tomatoes are outside, near the fruit."

At the till, the girl says, "Eighteen thousand sums, please." I give her my money and she gives me two thousand sums back. I buy a small sweet for myself with that money. At home my mother says, "Thank you, Rustam. You are a great helper." Then I sit in the kitchen and eat my sweet. Next Saturday I want to go to the shop again.

items.prompt: What is the name of the shop?
items.passage:
There is a new clothes shop in my street. It opens on Monday and its name is Fashion Land. My friend Nilufar and I walk there after school. The shop has big windows, and there are many bright clothes in them. A sign on the door says: "Everything is cheaper this week."

Inside, the shop is very big. There are two floors. Clothes for women are on the first floor and clothes for children are on the second floor. I look at the dresses. There is a long blue dress and a short red dress. Nilufar wants a yellow T-shirt. Her favourite colour is yellow. A young shop assistant helps us. Her name is Kamola.

I try on the blue dress. It is too big, so Kamola brings a smaller one. This dress is perfect! It costs one hundred and twenty thousand sums, but this week it is eighty thousand. I do not have enough money. I have only fifty thousand sums. Kamola says, "Come back on Friday, and we keep the dress for you." That is very kind.

Nilufar buys her yellow T-shirt for thirty thousand sums. We take photos in front of the shop and we go home. On Friday my father gives me thirty thousand sums, and I buy the blue dress. I wear it to school on Monday and everybody says it is beautiful.

There is a new clothes shop in my street. It opens on Monday and its name is Fashion Land. My friend Nilufar and I walk there after school. The shop has big windows, and there are many bright clothes in them. A sign on the door says: "Everything is cheaper this week."

Inside, the shop is very big. There are two floors. Clothes for women are on the first floor and clothes for children are on the second floor. I look at the dresses. There is a long blue dress and a short red dress. Nilufar wants a yellow T-shirt. Her favourite colour is yellow. A young shop assistant helps us. Her name is Kamola.

I try on the blue dress. It is too big, so Kamola brings a smaller one. This dress is perfect! It costs one hundred and twenty thousand sums, but this week it is eighty thousand. I do not have enough money. I have only fifty thousand sums. Kamola says, "Come back on Friday, and we keep the dress for you." That is very kind.

Nilufar buys her yellow T-shirt for thirty thousand sums. We take photos in front of the shop and we go home. On Friday my father gives me thirty thousand sums, and I buy the blue dress. I wear it to school on Monday and everybody says it is beautiful.

items.prompt: What is Mr Brown's job?
items.passage:
Hello, I am Mr Brown, an English teacher. Today I talk about breakfast around the world. Breakfast is the first meal of the day, and people eat very different things in different countries.

In England, many people eat eggs, bacon, toast and beans. They drink tea with milk. In Japan, breakfast is often rice, fish and soup. People there also drink green tea. In France, breakfast is very small. People eat a croissant and drink coffee. They do not eat much in the morning.

In Uzbekistan, breakfast is often bread with butter, cheese and tea. Some families eat hot soup or eggs with tomatoes. In Mexico, people like tortillas with beans and eggs. In Turkey, breakfast is big and has olives, cheese, tomatoes, eggs and bread. Families sit at the table for a long time and talk.

In my class there are twenty students. I ask them, "What do you eat for breakfast?" Twelve students say bread and tea. Five students say eggs. Three students eat nothing! I tell them that breakfast is important because it gives you energy for school. My favourite breakfast is a bowl of porridge with honey. What is yours?

items.prompt: How old is Sevara?
items.passage:
Tomorrow is my sister's birthday. Her name is Sevara and she is seven years old. I am Jasur and I am twelve. I want to make a cake for her. I can bake a little. My mother says I can use the kitchen after lunch.

I need flour, sugar, eggs, butter and milk. We have flour, sugar and milk at home, but there are no eggs. So I go to the shop and buy six eggs. I also buy strawberries and a small bottle of cream. Then I start. I put the butter and sugar in a bowl and mix them. Next I add the eggs, the flour and the milk. The mix looks yellow and soft.

I pour it into a round tin, and my mother puts the tin in the oven. We bake the cake for thirty-five minutes. While it is in the oven, I make the cream. I wash the strawberries and cut them in halves. When the cake is cool, I cover it with cream and put the strawberries on top. I also write "Happy Birthday Sevara" with chocolate.

The next day, at six o'clock, all our family sits in the living room. I bring the cake and put seven candles on it. Sevara closes her eyes and makes a wish. Then she blows out the candles. She says, "This is the best cake in the world!" Everyone has a big piece. I feel very proud and happy.

items.prompt: When does the supermarket close?
items.passage:
On Saturday morning, my father and I go to the supermarket. My name is Malika. The supermarket is a big building with a large car park. It is open from eight in the morning to eleven at night. On Saturdays it is full of families, and we need a trolley.

My father has a list. First, we go to the fruit and vegetable part. We buy bananas, oranges and potatoes. Then we go to the milk and cheese part. It is cold there, so I put on my jacket. Next to it is the meat part, and a man in a white hat cuts the meat for people. My father buys one kilo of beef.

I love the sweet part best. There are biscuits, chocolates and many kinds of juice. My father says, "You can choose one thing." I take a small orange juice. We also see a special offer on rice: two bags for the price of one. My father is happy and takes four bags.

At the till, there is a long line. We wait for ten minutes. My father pays with his card. A boy helps us put the shopping into bags. Outside, we put the bags in the car. On the way home, I drink my juice and look at the cars. Shopping on Saturday is tiring, but it is fun.

My father has a list. First, we go to the fruit and vegetable part. We buy bananas, oranges and potatoes. Then we go to the milk and cheese part. It is cold there, so I put on my jacket. Next to it is the meat part, and a man in a white hat cuts the meat for people. My father buys one kilo of beef.

I love the sweet part best. There are biscuits, chocolates and many kinds of juice. My father says, "You can choose one thing." I take a small orange juice. We also see a special offer on rice: two bags for the price of one. My father is happy and takes four bags.

At the till, there is a long line. We wait for ten minutes. My father pays with his card. A boy helps us put the shopping into bags. Outside, we put the bags in the car. On the way home, I drink my juice and look at the cars. Shopping on Saturday is tiring, but it is fun.

items.prompt: Where is the Blue Cup cafe?
items.passage:
My name is Akmal. Look at the menu of the Blue Cup cafe. It is a small cafe in Bukhara, and it opens at nine in the morning and closes at nine in the evening. My aunt Feruza works there as a cook, so I know the menu very well.

The menu has three parts. The first part is hot drinks. Black tea costs five thousand sums, coffee costs eight thousand sums, and hot chocolate costs ten thousand sums. The second part is food. There are sandwiches, soup, pasta and pizza. A cheese sandwich costs twelve thousand sums, and a big pizza costs thirty thousand sums.

The third part is sweet food. There is apple cake, ice cream and honey pancakes. The ice cream has three flavours: vanilla, chocolate and strawberry. Children love it. My aunt says the apple cake is her special recipe, and she uses her grandmother's old book. There is also a small sign on the wall. It says, "Please do not use your phone at the table."

Last Saturday, I go to the cafe with my friends Otabek and Sardor. I order a cheese sandwich and hot chocolate. Otabek takes a pizza, and Sardor orders pasta with a glass of cold water. After lunch, Aunt Feruza gives each of us a free piece of apple cake. We eat it and say it is the best cake in Bukhara.

items.prompt: What is wrong with Madina's old shoes?
items.answer: They are too small and have a hole
items.passage:
My old shoes are too small, and they have a hole in one of them. My father says, "Madina, today we go and buy new shoes." It is Thursday and the shoe shop is near our house. We go there after dinner.

The shop has many kinds of shoes. There are black school shoes, white trainers, brown boots and pink sandals. A tall man says, "Good evening! Can I help you?" My father says, "We need school shoes for my daughter." The man asks, "What size are you?" I do not know my size. He measures my foot with a metal tool. I am size thirty-three.

He brings three pairs of black shoes. The first pair is too tight. The second pair is too long. The third pair is perfect. They are comfortable and soft. I walk in the shop, and I can run in them too! The price is two hundred and fifty thousand sums. My father says it is a lot, but good shoes last a long time.

Then I see white trainers with a blue line. I really want them, and I look at my father with big eyes. He laughs and says, "Not today. Maybe for your birthday in May." I say OK. We pay for the school shoes and the man puts my old shoes in a green bag. I wear my new shoes home. I cannot wait to show my friends tomorrow.
options: They are too small and have a hole

items.prompt: Where does the class go for the picnic?
items.passage:
Next Saturday our class goes on a picnic to the Chimgan mountains. Our teacher, Ms Dilfuza, says every student must bring something to eat. I am Timur and I help my mother pack the picnic basket on Friday evening.

We have a big brown basket with a red cloth inside. First, we put in a blanket for sitting on the grass. Then my mother makes eight sandwiches with cheese and cucumber. She puts them in a box. We also put in six boiled eggs, a bag of apples and a bunch of grapes. There is a big bottle of water, but there is no juice. My mother says water is better for a hot day.

My mother says, "Do not forget the plates, the cups and the napkins." I also take a ball and a small cake for my friends. At the end, we put a knife for the apples in the basket. The basket is very heavy! My father says he can carry it to the bus.

On Saturday the weather is sunny and warm. The bus leaves at eight o'clock. After a one-hour trip, we arrive at the mountains. We find a nice place near a small river. We eat our food, play football and sing songs. My friend Bekzod forgets his water, so I give him half of my bottle. At four o'clock we clean the grass and take all our rubbish home. It is a lovely day.

items.prompt: What is Dr Nodira's job?
items.passage:
My name is Dr Nodira, and I am a children's doctor. Today I want to talk about healthy and unhealthy food. Healthy food helps your body and makes you strong. Unhealthy food tastes good, but it is not good for you every day.

Healthy food is fruit, vegetables, fish, eggs, milk and brown bread. Apples, carrots and tomatoes have vitamins. Milk and cheese are good for your bones and teeth. Fish and eggs help you to grow. You should eat five kinds of fruit and vegetables every day. You should also drink six glasses of water.

Unhealthy food is sweets, chips, fizzy drinks and fast food. These have a lot of sugar, salt or oil. A small bottle of fizzy drink has about seven spoons of sugar! If you eat too many sweets, your teeth hurt and you can feel sleepy. But you can eat sweets sometimes. A piece of cake on Sunday is OK.

Here is my advice. Eat breakfast every morning. Do not eat while you watch TV. Take fruit to school, not chips. Brush your teeth twice a day. And play outside for one hour every day. One of my patients, a boy called Sherzod, ate chips every day. Now he eats an apple at school and he feels much better. Remember: a healthy body is a happy body.

items.prompt: What is the name of the bakery?
items.passage:
My uncle has a small bakery in Namangan. It is called Golden Bread. He gets up at three o'clock every morning, because the bread must be ready at six. My name is Sanjar, and in the summer holidays I help him.

At the bakery, there are three workers. Uncle Karim makes the dough with flour, water, salt and yeast. Mr Olim puts the dough into the big oven. The oven is very hot, and the bread cooks for about twenty minutes. Mrs Gavhar makes cakes and sweet buns with sugar and nuts. The smell is wonderful, and people stand outside the door before we open.

We sell many things. Round bread called non costs three thousand sums. Long white bread costs four thousand sums. A sweet bun costs two thousand sums, and a big chocolate cake costs fifty thousand sums. My job is easy. I put the bread in paper bags and say thank you to the customers. I also clean the tables at the end of the day.

My favourite customer is an old man named Mr Tursun. Every day he buys two non and one bun. He always gives me a small gift, for example a pencil or a sweet. On Fridays, my uncle gives bread to poor families, and he does not take any money. I think my uncle is a very good man. One day I want to have my own bakery too.

items.prompt: Where is Mr Rahim's stall?
items.passage:
Mr Rahim is a fruit seller. He has a small stall in front of our school in Andijan. He is fifty years old, and he works there every day from eight in the morning to six in the evening. I am Aziza, and I stop at his stall every afternoon.

His stall is always neat and colourful. There are oranges, bananas, pears, plums and big green watermelons. In summer he also has sweet cherries and peaches. Each fruit has a small sign with a price. Bananas cost twelve thousand sums for a kilo, and apples cost eight thousand sums. Mr Rahim says, "Good fruit is not cheap, but it is worth it."

He knows his fruit very well. He can tell if a melon is sweet when he knocks on it. He tells us to wash the fruit before we eat it. He also shows us how to keep bananas fresh. We should put them in a cool and dry place, away from other fruit.

One day it rains very hard, and the street is empty. I see Mr Rahim under a big blue umbrella. He is alone and cold. I run home and ask my mother for a cup of hot tea. I bring it to him. He is very happy and gives me three big red apples for my family. Now we are good friends, and my mother also buys fruit from him every week.

Next Sunday is Mother's Day, and I want to buy a gift for my mum. My name is Laylo and I am eleven. I have fifty thousand sums in my money box. I save it for two months. My brother Doniyor says he can come with me to the shopping centre.

On Saturday we take the bus to the centre. It is big and busy, with many shops. First, we look in a flower shop. Red roses are very beautiful, but they cost ten thousand sums for one flower. That is too much. Then we visit a shop for bags. A brown bag is nice, but it costs ninety thousand sums. Doniyor says, "Mum has two bags already."

In the next shop there are scarves. I find a soft green scarf with small white flowers. Green is my mother's favourite colour. The price is forty-five thousand sums. I take it to the shop assistant, and she puts it in a pretty box with a pink ribbon. I also buy a card for five thousand sums, so I have no money left.

On Sunday morning, I make breakfast with Doniyor. We put the box and the card next to her tea. My mother comes in and sees the gift. She opens the box and her eyes are full of tears. She hugs us and says, "This is the best gift in the world." She wears the scarf all day. I learn something important: a gift does not need to be expensive. It needs love.

Next Sunday is Mother's Day, and I want to buy a gift for my mum. My name is Laylo and I am eleven. I have fifty thousand sums in my money box. I save it for two months. My brother Doniyor says he can come with me to the shopping centre.

On Saturday we take the bus to the centre. It is big and busy, with many shops. First, we look in a flower shop. Red roses are very beautiful, but they cost ten thousand sums for one flower. That is too much. Then we visit a shop for bags. A brown bag is nice, but it costs ninety thousand sums. Doniyor says, "Mum has two bags already."

In the next shop there are scarves. I find a soft green scarf with small white flowers. Green is my mother's favourite colour. The price is forty-five thousand sums. I take it to the shop assistant, and she puts it in a pretty box with a pink ribbon. I also buy a card for five thousand sums, so I have no money left.

On Sunday morning, I make breakfast with Doniyor. We put the box and the card next to her tea. My mother comes in and sees the gift. She opens the box and her eyes are full of tears. She hugs us and says, "This is the best gift in the world." She wears the scarf all day. I learn something important: a gift does not need to be expensive. It needs love.

items.prompt: Where does Nodira live?
items.passage:
My name is Nodira. I live in Samarkand with my family. I want to tell you about my town centre. It is small, but it is very nice.

In the middle of the centre there is a big square. There is a fountain in the square, and there are many old trees. Children play there after school. On Sundays, there is a small market near the fountain. People sell fruit, bread and flowers. My mother buys apples there every week. They are cheap and very sweet.

There are two banks, one library and three cafes in the centre. The library is behind the square. It opens at nine o'clock and it closes at six. I go there on Tuesdays and Thursdays. I read books and do my homework. My brother Aziz does not like books. He likes the sports shop next to the bank. It has football shoes and red bags.

My favourite place is a small cafe called Sunrise. It is on the corner. The owner is Mr Karimov. He is very kind. I drink tea there with my friend Malika. We eat a cake and we talk for one hour. The cafe is open every day, but it is closed on New Year's Day.

There is no cinema in the centre. It is far away, and we go there by bus. But I like my town centre. It is clean, quiet and friendly. Come and visit me one day!

items.prompt: Where does Bobur live?
items.passage:
Today is Saturday, and I am on the bus. My name is Bobur. I live in Tashkent. I go to my grandmother's house every weekend. Her house is near the zoo. I take bus number twelve.

The bus stop is in front of my school. The bus comes at a quarter past eight. Today it is a little late. There are many people at the stop. A young woman has a big blue bag. An old man has a newspaper. I buy my ticket from the driver. It costs one thousand four hundred sum.

The bus is full. There is no free seat, so I stand near the door. After two stops, an old man gets up. He says, "Please, sit here, boy." I say, "No, thank you. You are older." But he smiles and I sit down. I say thank you.

The journey is thirty-five minutes. There are nine stops. I look out of the window. I see a big mosque, a park and a small market. A girl next to me listens to music. Her name is Madina. She goes to the zoo with her little sister.

At last I see the zoo. I push the red button. The bus stops and I get off. My grandmother waits at the corner. She has a small brown dog, Max. He is happy to see me. We walk home and drink tea.

items.prompt: Who is the letter to?
items.passage:
Dear Emma,

Thank you for your letter. I am happy that you visit Bukhara next week. You ask about the city museum. It is easy to find, and I can tell you the way.

Your hotel is on Navoi Street. When you leave the hotel, turn left. Walk past the pharmacy and the small bakery. After about two hundred metres, you see a bridge. Cross the bridge. On the other side, there is a blue school. Turn right at the school. Then go straight for five minutes.

You see a big park on your left. The museum is next to the park. It is a tall red building with a green door. There is a statue of a horse in front of it. You cannot miss it!

The museum opens at ten in the morning and closes at five. It is closed on Mondays, so please do not go on that day. A ticket costs twenty thousand sum. There is a small cafe inside. The tea is good and the cakes are cheap. There are old maps, coins and carpets in the museum. My favourite room is the one with the big blue plates.

If you do not want to walk, you can take a taxi. It costs only ten thousand sum. I am at work on Wednesday, but on Thursday I am free. I can go to the museum with you.

See you soon!

Your friend,
Sardor

items.prompt: What time does Kamila wake up?
items.passage:
Hello, friends! My name is Kamila and I am in Tashkent for one day. This is my story.

I wake up at seven o'clock. My hotel is near the centre. I have breakfast in the hotel. I eat bread, eggs and cheese, and I drink black tea. At eight thirty, I walk to the metro station. The metro is clean and fast. It costs only a few coins.

First, I go to Chorsu Bazaar. It is very big and very busy. There are many shops with nuts, dried fruit and spices. A kind seller gives me one sweet apricot. I buy two bags of nuts for my mother. Then I buy a small blue hat for my brother. It is cheap.

At one o'clock, I am hungry. I eat plov in a small restaurant near the bazaar. The plov is hot and very tasty. The waiter is a young man called Otabek. He speaks English, and he is very friendly.

In the afternoon, I go to Amir Temur Square. There is a large statue and a beautiful garden. There are many flowers, and many families sit on the benches. I take about fifty photos.

In the evening, I am tired, but I am happy. I take the metro back to the hotel at six. Tashkent is a great city. There is so much to see here. I want to come again next summer.

items.prompt: What time is Jasur's plane?
items.passage:
It is five o'clock in the morning. My name is Jasur, and I am at home with two big bags. My plane is at eight o'clock. I do not want to be late, so I call a taxi.

The taxi comes in ten minutes. It is a white car. The driver is a tall man called Mr Rustam. He says, "Good morning! Where do you want to go?" I say, "To the airport, please." He puts my bags in the back of the car and we go.

The streets are quiet. There are only a few cars and a few buses. It is still dark, and the street lights are yellow. Mr Rustam has a small radio. He plays soft music. He asks me, "Do you like music?" I say, "Yes, I do, very much."

After fifteen minutes, there is a problem. There is a lot of traffic near the big bridge. A truck is stopped on the road. Mr Rustam is not angry. He says, "Don't worry. I know a short way." He turns right into a small street. It is fast and we are on the main road again.

We arrive at the airport at twenty to six. The ride is twenty-five minutes. The price is forty thousand sum. I give Mr Rustam fifty thousand and I say, "Keep the rest." He smiles and says, "Thank you! Have a good trip."

My name is Gulnora. I am ten years old. I live on Gul Street in a small town. It is a short street, but it is my favourite place. Let me tell you about it.

There are twelve houses on my street. Our house is number seven. It is yellow, and it has a green gate. There is a small garden in front of it. My father has a big apple tree and my mother has roses. Next to us live Mrs Salima and her cat, Mimi. Mimi is white and very fat. She sleeps on the wall all day.

At the beginning of the street, there is a bakery. It opens very early, at five o'clock. In the morning, the whole street smells of fresh bread. I go there every day before school. I buy two warm loaves for one thousand five hundred sum. The baker, Mr Ahmad, always gives me a small piece of sweet bread.

At the end of the street, there is my school. It is only five minutes on foot. I walk with my friends Laylo and Sevara. We talk and laugh all the way.

The street is very quiet. There are not many cars. In the evening, children play football and old men play chess on a bench. I love my street. I think it is the best street in the world.

items.prompt: Where does Timur go?
items.passage:
My name is Timur. Today I go to Bukhara with my father. We take the train, and I am very excited. I love trains.

We arrive at the railway station at seven o'clock in the morning. Our train leaves at seven thirty. The station is big and busy. There are many people with bags, and there is a loud voice on the speakers. It says the train numbers and the platforms.

First, we go to the ticket office. My father has our tickets already, but he wants to check them. A woman at the window says, "Your train is on platform three." We thank her and go there. On the way, my father buys a bottle of water and two sandwiches in a small shop.

The train is long and blue. It is new and clean. Our seats are in carriage five, seats twelve and thirteen. I sit next to the window. There is a small table in front of me, and I put my book on it.

The train leaves exactly on time. It is fast. The journey is four hours. I look at the fields, the villages and the mountains. A kind man in the next seat shares his apples with us. In the end, we arrive in Bukhara at half past eleven. My grandfather waits for us on the platform. He is very happy to see us.

items.prompt: Who is Jina?
items.passage:
Today I go to the post office. My name is Dilnoza. I want to send a letter and a small parcel to my cousin in Korea. Her name is Jina. It is her birthday next week.

The post office is on Mustaqillik Street, near the bank. It is a white building with a blue sign. It opens at eight o'clock in the morning and it closes at five in the afternoon. On Sundays, it is closed. I arrive at half past nine.

There are five people in front of me. I wait for ten minutes. There is a small table with pens and paper. I write the address on the parcel with a black pen. It is a long address and I write it very carefully.

Then it is my turn. The clerk is a friendly young woman. Her name is Ms Zarina. I give her the parcel. In it, there is a book about Uzbekistan, a scarf and some dried apricots. She puts the parcel on a scale. It is one kilogram. She says, "It costs sixty thousand sum."

I also buy a stamp for my letter. It costs five thousand sum. Ms Zarina says, "The parcel takes about ten days to get there." I say, "That is good. It is not late." I pay, say thank you, and leave. I hope Jina likes my present.

items.passage:
Mark is a tourist from Canada. He is in Samarkand for two days. It is his first morning, and he stands in front of his hotel with a city map. He is a little lost.

On the map, Mark sees a river in the north and a big park in the south. The railway station is in the west. The old square, the Registan, is in the centre. There are small red circles on the map. They show the best places for tourists. There are twelve circles, and Mark wants to see five of them.

A girl is near him. Her name is Lola. She is a student, and she speaks good English. She says, "Can I help you?" Mark says, "Yes, please. Where is the Registan?" Lola looks at the map and says, "We are here, at the hotel. The Registan is only ten minutes on foot. Go straight, and turn left at the big clock."

Mark asks, "Is there a bank near here?" Lola says, "Yes, there is one next to the post office. Look, it is here on your map." She uses a pen and makes a blue cross.

Mark says, "Thank you very much! You are very kind." Lola smiles and says, "You are welcome. Enjoy my city!" Mark puts the map in his pocket and walks to the Registan. Now he is not lost, and he is very happy.

items.prompt: Who goes to the park with Anvar?
items.passage:
On Sunday, I go for a walk in the park with my grandfather. My name is Anvar. My grandfather's name is Ibrahim. He is seventy years old, but he is very strong. He walks every day.

The park is not far from our house. It takes ten minutes on foot. It is a very big park with a lake in the middle. There are tall trees and many flowers. The air is fresh and cool. It is a sunny morning, and the birds sing.

First, we walk around the lake. It is two kilometres long. There are ducks on the water, and I have some bread for them. Grandfather says, "Don't give them too much!" We laugh. A little white duck comes very near. I think it is hungry.

Then we see some boys. They play football on the grass. One of them is my friend Sanjar. He says hello and I wave. There is also an old man with a small dog. The dog runs very fast.

After one hour, we are tired. We sit on a bench under a big tree. Grandfather buys two ice creams from a man with a cart. Mine is chocolate and his is vanilla. We sit and talk for a long time. Grandfather tells me about the park when he was a boy. There was no lake then, only a small river. I love my Sundays with him.

There is a new bridge in our town, Namangan. It opened last Friday, and everybody is talking about it. I am a reporter, and this is my report.

The bridge is over the Syr Darya river. It is three hundred metres long and twenty metres wide. It has two lanes for cars and a wide path for people. At night, there are blue and white lights on it. It is very beautiful. The builders worked for two years. About one hundred and fifty people built it.

Before, there was only a small old bridge. It was narrow and it was very slow. There were always too many cars on it. Many people waited for half an hour. Now, the trip takes only ten minutes. Students can get to the university early, and farmers can bring their fruit to the market faster.

On Friday, there was a big party at the bridge. The mayor, Mr Yusupov, cut a red ribbon. Many children ran across the bridge. A band played music, and there was free tea for everybody. I talked with an old woman named Halima. She said, "I am happy. Now I can visit my sister in one short ride."

The town is proud of its new bridge. Next summer, the mayor wants to build a small park next to it. I think it is a great idea.

items.prompt: Where is Aziza's home?
items.passage:
My name is Aziza. I am a student in Tashkent, and I take the metro every day. For me, it is the best way to travel in the city.

My home is in the south, and my university is in the centre. The metro takes me there in twenty minutes. A bus takes one hour because of the traffic. I get on at Chilonzor station at a quarter to eight. The metro is cheap, too. A ticket costs one thousand four hundred sum.

The stations are very beautiful. Some of them are like small museums. I love Alisher Navoi station. It is blue and gold, and it has big lamps and pictures on the walls. Many tourists take photos there. Kosmonavtlar station has pictures of space and stars. It is my little brother's favourite.

The trains come every five minutes in the morning. They are clean and quiet. In the morning, there are many people, and I often stand. But I do not mind. I read a book or listen to music. In the evening, the train is less full, and I can sit.

There are some rules in the metro. Do not run on the stairs. Stand on the right side of the escalator. Give your seat to old people and to mothers with small children. Also, you cannot eat on the train. I think these rules are good. The metro is clean because people follow them.

My name is Rustam, and I am twelve years old. I love bikes. This month, there is great news in my town. There is a new bike lane on Bahor Street!

The bike lane is four kilometres long. It starts at the railway station and goes to the big park. It is green, so cars can see it easily. There is a white line between the bike lane and the road. There are also small signs with a picture of a bike. The workers built it in only six weeks.

Before, I rode my bike on the pavement. It was not safe, and people were angry with me. Now I ride on the bike lane every day. I go to school on my bike. It takes eight minutes. My sister Nilufar rides with me. She is only nine, but she rides very well. Our mother says, "Use your helmets!" We always do.

There are many new bikers now. Fifty children from my school ride to class. There is a small bike shop near the park, and it is always busy. The owner, Mr Botir, says, "I sell ten bikes a week now. Last year, I sold two."

I think a bike lane is good for the town. It is quiet and clean. There is less traffic and less smoke. People are healthy and happy. I hope there is a bike lane in every street one day.
